title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: BEV'S HARDWARE
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Bev Kowalski, a hardware store owner in Tucson, Arizona.
Six aisles, and one cat named Wrench.
Then a giant warehouse store opened two miles away. Forty aisles.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: FORTY AISLES
segments.quote: Change is the law of life. And those who look only to the past or present are certain to miss the future.
segments.author: John F. Kennedy
lines: Bev's sales fell by half. She spent her days staring at an empty parking lot.
Above the register hung her dad's old clipping of a speech by President Kennedy:
Change is the law of life. And those who look only to the past or present are certain to miss the future.
Bev decided to stop staring.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: THE PRICE WAR
segments.quote: It is better to offer no excuse than a bad one.
segments.author: George Washington
lines: First, she tried to beat the big store on price. She lost money every week, and blamed everything. The warehouse. The heat.
Her husband Ray, a history buff, read her a line from George Washington:
It is better to offer no excuse than a bad one.
So Bev stopped blaming, and asked customers what they needed. The answer? Someone who knows how to fix things.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: SOMEDAY SATURDAY
segments.quote: Lost time is never found again.
segments.author: Benjamin Franklin
lines: So she planned free fix-it lessons on Saturdays. But she kept saying, after the holidays.
Then she found her dad's old Ben Franklin almanac, with one line underlined:
Lost time is never found again.
That Saturday, she taught leaky faucets. Two people came. Three, if you count the cat.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: THE BIG HEAD
segments.quote: Success is a lousy teacher. It seduces smart people into thinking they can't lose.
segments.author: Bill Gates
lines: By spring, forty people packed the store every Saturday. And Bev got a little full of herself.
She rolled her eyes at a nervous young dad. He walked out.
That night, Ray read her a line from Bill Gates:
Success is a lousy teacher. It seduces smart people into thinking they can't lose.
Bev called the young dad, said sorry, and started a beginners' class.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: MONSOON SEASON
segments.quote: It is thrifty to prepare today for the wants of tomorrow.
segments.author: Aesop
lines: In May, a hundred and five degrees and bone dry, Bev ordered a mountain of tarps. Ray said she was crazy.
She quoted Aesop, the ancient Greek storyteller:
It is thrifty to prepare today for the wants of tomorrow.
In July, the monsoon hit. The warehouse sold out in an hour. Bev's shelves stayed full.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: THE BIG GUY
segments.quote: The best revenge is not to be like your enemy.
segments.author: Marcus Aurelius
lines: Next morning, in walked Greg, the warehouse manager, soaking wet. His own roof was leaking.
Bev was tempted to charge him double. Then she remembered the Roman emperor Marcus Aurelius:
The best revenge is not to be like your enemy.
So she charged the normal price, and showed him how to patch it. Now a sign at the warehouse says: Tricky problem? Ask Bev.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Welcome change. No excuses. Start now. Stay humble. Prepare early. Be kind to rivals.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Welcome change. Drop the excuses. Start now. Stay humble. Prepare early. And be kind, even to rivals.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night. And if anyone can fix my faucet, call me.
